problem: Quality and customer connection had weakened.
title: Starbucks closes about 7,100 stores for an afternoon to retrain baristas
context: Starbucks leadership believed espresso quality had slipped as the company grew.
decision_made: Close company-operated US stores for several hours to retrain about 135,000 employees.
action_taken: Staff watched a video from CEO Howard Schultz and practised espresso standards on 26 February 2008.
observed_outcome: Not documented in the sources used. A rival ran a 99-cent coffee promotion that day.
lessons: A visible, costly signal can show seriousness about quality, but its effects are hard to measure.
limitations: Closure hours differ by source. Sales and quality effects were not found.

claims.claim_text: Starbucks closed about 7,100 US stores for an afternoon to retrain employees on espresso.
Schultz described the move as admitting that espresso quality had slipped.
